n3b5be2eb6dc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan houses?
o: Rooms were arranged round a central courtyard.
Staircases show that houses could be multi-storeyed.
Many houses at Mohenjodaro had their own wells.
Doors and windows usually opened onto the main streets.
n3b5be2eb6dc.x: Doors and windows opened onto side lanes, not main streets. Courtyard plans, staircases and wells inside houses are all attested.

na6e215a2790.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan town planning?
o: The cities displayed a grid pattern.
Public buildings were generally associated with the citadel.
The same size of brick was used for every construction.
The main streets were about 10 metres wide.
na6e215a2790.x: Brick sizes differed by construction (house bricks about 7 × 14 × 28 cm, city-wall bricks about 10 × 20 × 40 cm), though all followed the same ratio.

n76e4d05c824.s: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro had flights of steps at its:
n76e4d05c824.x: The Great Bath had flights of steps at its north and south ends; it is mostly read as a place for ritual bathing.

nb7c648254a1.s: Which animal is absent from Harappan seals and figurines?
nb7c648254a1.x: The lion does not appear on Harappan seals or figurines, while the unicorn, elephant and rhinoceros do.

n15dc04d6a08.s: Which Harappan settlement in Afghanistan functioned as a trading colony for lapis lazuli?
n15dc04d6a08.x: Shortughai, in Afghanistan, was a trading colony for lapis lazuli. Sutkagendor was on the Makran coast, Balakot on the Sindh coast and Lothal in Gujarat.

n6d627c87245.s: Which of the following did the Harappans import?
n6d627c87245.x: Silver was imported; carnelian beads, ivory, timber and cotton were exports.

n58ea77de544.s: According to the accepted view, which animal was NOT known to the Mature Harappans?
n58ea77de544.x: The horse was not known to the Mature Harappans in the accepted view; the Surkotada claims are controversial. Sequence was not possible as the facts carry no dates.

new.s: In Mohenjodaro and Harappa, the streets ran in which directions?
o: North-south and east-west, crossing at right angles
Only north-south, parallel to the river
In curving lanes with no fixed pattern
new.x: Streets ran north-south and east-west and crossed at right angles, dividing the cities into blocks.

new.s: The main streets of Harappan cities were approximately how wide?
new.x: Main streets were about 10 m (30 feet) wide.

new.s: Which of the following has NOT been clearly found in Harappan cities, unlike Mesopotamia and Egypt?
new.x: No temples or palaces have been clearly found in IVC cities, though granaries, covered drains and wells exist.

new.s: The Indus Valley Civilization belongs to which age?
new.x: The IVC was a Bronze Age culture; iron came much later, around 1000 BC.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an Indus Valley site?
new.x: Pataliputra is not an IVC site; Kalibangan, Ropar and Lothal are.

new.s: At which Harappan site was the lower town also fortified?
new.x: Kalibangan had a citadel and a lower town that was also fortified.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Curved bricks are linked with Chanhudaro, ornamental bricks with Kalibangan and sandstone-limestone blocks with Dholavira.

new.s: Harappan house bricks measured approximately:
new.x: House bricks were about 7 × 14 × 28 cm; 10 × 20 × 40 cm was the size of city-wall bricks, both in the ratio 1:2:4.

new.s: Mud bricks, rather than burnt bricks, were notably used at which Harappan site?
new.x: Burnt bricks were common, but mud bricks were used for fillings and platforms and at Kalibangan.

new.s: Doors and windows of Harappan houses generally opened onto:
new.x: Doors and windows opened onto side lanes, not onto the main streets.

new.s: Staircases found in Harappan houses show that the houses were:
new.x: Staircases show that houses could be multi-storeyed; 'houses mostly single-storey' is a trap.

new.s: Waste water carried by covered Harappan street drains finally drained into:
new.x: House drains led to covered street drains with manholes, which emptied into soak pits or main channels.

new.s: Wooden drains are associated with which Harappan site?
new.x: Kalibangan had wooden drains, while Banawali had no systematic drainage.

new.s: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro was about how deep?
new.x: The Great Bath was about 12 m × 7 m and 2.4 m deep.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Bath:
1. It lay on the citadel mound of Mohenjodaro.
2. It measured about 12 m × 7 m.
3. It was about 7 m deep.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It was on the Mohenjodaro citadel mound and about 12 m × 7 m; its depth was only about 2.4 m, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: The pillared assembly hall of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
new.x: The pillared assembly hall is a Mohenjodaro structure.

new.s: How many fire altars were found at Kalibangan?
new.x: Kalibangan yielded seven fire altars; fire altars are also known from Lothal.

new.s: The dockyard, the only proof of a Harappan port, was found at:
new.x: The tidal dockyard is at Lothal, not Harappa.

new.s: Granaries arranged in two rows of six near the river were found at:
new.x: Harappa had a granary of 12 rooms in two rows of six near the river; the Great Granary on the citadel was at Mohenjodaro.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: The dockyard is at Lothal, not Harappa; horse bones are from Surkotada and the bronze chariot from Daimabad.

new.s: How many reservoirs, covering about 10% of the site, were found at Dholavira?
new.x: Dholavira had 16 reservoirs, about 10% of the site, some of them rock-cut.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Dholavira:
1. It is one of the five largest Harappan cities.
2. Its huge rock-cut reservoir was about 79 m × 12 m.
3. It was built mainly of baked bricks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Dholavira was one of the five largest cities and had a 79 m × 12 m rock-cut reservoir; it used sandstone and limestone blocks, not baked brick.

new.s: Harappa, the first Indus site to be excavated (1921), was dug by:
new.x: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; R.D. Banerji dug Mohenjodaro in 1922.

new.s: In which year did R.D. Banerji excavate Mohenjodaro?
new.x: Mohenjodaro was excavated by R.D. Banerji in 1922, a year after Harappa.

new.s: Lothal was excavated by:
new.x: S.R. Rao excavated Lothal (1954-57), as asked in APPSC 2018.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of site and excavator is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Banawali was excavated by R.S. Bisht; S.R. Rao excavated Lothal.

new.s: Which was the first Harappan site excavated after Independence?
new.x: Ropar, dug by Y.D. Sharma in 1955-56, was the first site excavated after Independence.

new.s: Kalibangan is located in which district of Rajasthan?
new.x: Kalibangan, on the Ghaggar, is in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan (APPSC 2018).

new.s: Harappa is situated on the banks of which river?
new.x: Harappa lies on the Ravi in Punjab (Pakistan); Mohenjodaro is on the Indus.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Ropar is on the Sutlej; Lothal is on the Bhogava/Sabarmati, Kalibangan on the Ghaggar and Rangpur on the Sukhbhadar.

new.s: Rakhigarhi, the largest Harappan site in India, is in:
new.x: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar, Haryana, not Rajasthan; Fatehabad has Banawali.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mohenjodaro is in Larkana district of Sindh.
2. Banawali is in Fatehabad district of Haryana.
3. Lothal stands on the Ravi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Mohenjodaro is in Larkana and Banawali in Fatehabad; Lothal is on the Bhogava/Sabarmati, not the Ravi.

new.s: The earliest ploughed field, with criss-cross furrows (c. 2800 BC), was found at:
new.x: Kalibangan has the earliest ploughed field; Banawali has a toy (terracotta) plough.

new.s: A bead factory with a furnace and carnelian drills was found at:
new.x: Chanhudaro had a bead factory with furnace and carnelian drills; bead-making is also seen at Lothal.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Fire altars are a Kalibangan find; Banawali is known for a toy plough and radial streets.

new.s: The Pashupati seal, showing a three-faced figure in yogic posture ringed by animals, was found at:
new.x: The Pashupati ('Proto-Shiva') seal is from Mohenjodaro.

new.s: The ship seal and the Persian Gulf seal were found at:
new.x: Lothal yielded the ship seal, the Persian Gulf seal and a copper dog.

new.s: Which tree is most commonly depicted on Harappan seals?
new.x: The pipal is the most depicted tree, while the unicorn is the most common seal motif.

new.s: The steatite bust known as the 'Priest-King' was found at:
new.x: The Priest-King steatite bust is from Mohenjodaro.

new.s: The brick-lined tidal dock at Lothal measures about:
new.x: Lothal's tidal dock is about 218 m × 37 m with sluice gates; 79 m × 12 m is Dholavira's rock-cut reservoir.

new.s: Cemetery R-37 and Cemetery H belong to which site?
new.x: Cemetery R-37, Cemetery H and coffin burial are from Harappa.

new.s: A dog buried with a human was found at:
new.x: Ropar has a dog buried with a human and oval pit burials.

new.s: A double burial of a man and a woman in one grave is a notable find from:
new.x: Lothal has a double (joint) burial of a man and woman; Rakhigarhi also shows double burials.

new.s: How many skeletons in all have been found in Rakhigarhi's Mound 7 cemetery?
new.x: Mound 7 at Rakhigarhi has yielded 56 skeletons, including a woman about 4,600 years old.

new.s: The Sindhi name 'Mohenjodaro' means:
new.x: Mohenjodaro means 'Mound of the Dead'; Kalibangan means 'black bangles'.

new.s: Kalibangan literally means:
new.x: Kalibangan means 'black bangles'.

new.s: Dholavira is locally known as:
new.x: Dholavira's local name is Kotada, meaning large fort.

new.s: Banawali shows how many cultural phases?
new.x: Banawali has three phases: pre-Harappan, Harappan and post-Harappan; seven stages belong to Dholavira.

new.s: When Dholavira was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021, it became India's:
new.x: Dholavira became India's 40th World Heritage Site in 2021 and is the only inscribed Harappan site in India.

new.s: The National Maritime Heritage Complex is being developed at which Harappan site?
new.x: The NMHC at Lothal was approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2024 under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

new.s: Which is the largest Harappan site in India?
new.x: Rakhigarhi, about 350 ha, is the largest Harappan site in India.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Harappan site?
new.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur, UP) is a Mauryan copper-plate site; the others are Harappan.

new.s: Sohgaura in Gorakhpur district is known for:
new.x: Sohgaura is not Harappan; it is known for a Mauryan-era copper plate about granaries for famine.

new.s: Which is the westernmost Harappan site?
new.x: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast of Pakistan is the westernmost Harappan site.

new.s: In Mesopotamian records, 'Dilmun' referred to:
new.x: Dilmun was Bahrain; Meluhha was the Indus region and Magan was Oman or Makran.

new.s: The Mesopotamian name 'Magan' is identified with:
new.x: Magan was Oman (or Makran); Dilmun was Bahrain.

new.s: In November 2025 a second Dilmun temple (c. 1900-1800 BCE) was found on which island?
new.x: The second Dilmun temple was found on Failaka island, Kuwait, in November 2025.

new.s: The Harappans obtained copper from:
new.x: Copper came from Khetri (Rajasthan) and Oman; gold came from Kolar and lapis lazuli from Badakhshan.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Gold came from Kolar; copper from Khetri, lapis lazuli from Badakhshan and chert from Rohri.

new.s: A terracotta plough model was found at:
new.x: Banawali has the terracotta plough model; Kalibangan has the ploughed field.

new.s: The earliest evidence of garlic comes from:
new.x: The earliest garlic is from Balu in Haryana; Rojdi is linked with indigo.

new.s: Rice husks, the first rice evidence in Gujarat (c. 1800 BCE), were found at:
new.x: Rice husks c. 1800 BCE come from Lothal and Rangpur.

new.s: Most Harappan seals were of which shape?
new.x: Most seals were square, carrying an animal and script; rectangular seals carry script only.

new.s: A cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif was found in June 2026 at:
new.x: In June 2026 a cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif and five characters was found at Rakhigarhi.

new.s: The basic unit of Harappan weights was approximately:
new.x: The weight unit was about 13.63 g, in a binary system with a ratio of 16.

new.s: A shell scale of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
new.x: The shell scale is from Mohenjodaro; the ivory scale is from Lothal and the copper scale from Harappa.

new.s: Which of the following animals is NOT depicted in Harappan art?
new.x: The cow is never depicted, while the unicorn, zebu bull and rhinoceros appear on seals.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The earliest furnace is at Kot Bala; salt was made at Kerala-no-dhoro, Kuntasi had ivory, copper and bead workshops, and Chanhudaro is the Lancashire of India.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan spinning:
1. Spindle-whorls are commonly found in houses.
2. A spinning wheel has been found at Harappan sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Spindle-whorls are common in houses, but no spinning wheel has been found.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Lothal dock was joined to the Gulf of Khambhat.
2. Harappa was a port on the Ravi.
3. Sutkagendor was the westernmost Harappan port.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Lothal's dock joined the Gulf of Khambhat and Sutkagendor was the westernmost port; Harappa was an inland city on the Ravi, not a port.

new.s: Which of the following was a Harappan export?
new.x: Timber, carnelian beads, ivory and cotton were exports; silver, tin and woollens were imports.
